doc_description: Best Buy Co., Inc.’s Form 10‑Q for the quarter ended July 29, 2023 (Q2 FY2024), filed Sept. 1, 2023, presents unaudited condensed consolidated financials and MD&A highlighting $9.6B revenue (-7.2%) with improved gross margin, $15.3B in assets, a new $1.25B revolving credit facility, continued use of a $5.0B share repurchase authorization ($3.975B remaining), and effective controls for NYSE: BBY.

structure.title: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.heading: Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase: Unless the context otherwise requires, the use of the terms “Best Buy ,” “we,” “us” and “our” refers to Best Buy Co., Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries.
structure.summary:
- Document type and scope: Excerpts from Best Buy Co., Inc.’s Form 10‑Q MD&A for Q2 FY2024 (three and six months ended July 29, 2023), including segment data, results of operations, non‑GAAP reconciliations, liquidity, market risk, controls, and other disclosures.

- Assets by segment: Total assets $15.3B; Domestic $14.0B; International $1.3B.

- Company overview and seasonality: Two segments (Domestic, including Best Buy Health; International/Canada). Fiscal year ends near end of January; Q4 is seasonally strongest.

- Comparable sales methodology: Definition covers stores/web/call centers ≥14 months; includes online sales regardless of fulfillment, credit card revenue, gift card breakage, commercial/wholesale where applicable; excludes stores closed >14 days until 14 months post‑reopen, discontinued ops, services plan profit‑share revenue, and FX impacts (International).

- Non‑GAAP measures: Use of constant currency, non‑GAAP operating income, effective tax rate, and diluted EPS; reconciliations provided; adjustments include restructuring, intangible amortization, acquisition/other items, investment gains/losses, and related tax effects.

- Business strategy update:
  - Omnichannel: Digital sales were 31% of Domestic revenue (consistent YoY; ~2x pre‑pandemic). ~40% of online orders picked up in stores.
  - Store portfolio: On track to close 20–30 large format stores in FY24, remodel 8 Experience stores, and expand Outlets to ~25.
  - Labor model: Reallocating labor to reflect channel shift, investing in flexible, multi‑skilled workforce; aim to balance customer experience with cost efficiency.
  - Membership: Relaunched program to offer more choice at lower cost to serve; early margin favorability.
  - Outlook: Expect FY24 industry sales decline amid inflation and higher rates; longer‑term growth drivers include upgrade cycles, vendor innovation, cloud/AR/AI/broadband, and expansion into wellness tech, personal e‑transportation, outdoor living, and EV charging.

- Consolidated results:
  - Revenue: Q2 $9.6B (-7.2%); 1H $19.1B (-9.2%); comps -6.2% and -8.2%, respectively.
  - Profitability: Gross margin rate up (Q2 23.2% vs 22.1%); SG&A rate up; operating margin Q2 flat at 3.6%, 1H down to 3.5% (from 4.0%).
  - EPS and taxes: Q2 diluted EPS $1.25 (vs $1.35); 1H $2.36 (vs $2.85). ETR increased (Q2 26.1% vs 15.6%) due to prior‑year discrete items; similar drivers for 1H.

- Domestic segment:
  - Revenue/Comps: Q2 revenue $8.89B (-7.1%), comps -6.3%; 1H revenue $17.69B (-9.1%), comps -8.4%.
  - Online: Q2 $2.76B (31% of segment; comp online -7.1%); 1H $5.45B (30.8%; -9.7%).
  - Category performance: Declines in appliances, home theater, computing, mobile phones; growth in gaming; services up on paid membership growth.
  - Margin drivers: Higher product margins, improved membership economics (including services) and Health margin; credit card profit‑share has aided margins in recent years (~1.4% of Domestic revenue in FY23) and expected to be neutral for FY24 overall.
  - SG&A: Q2 flat (higher incentives offset by lower store payroll); 1H down (lower store payroll offset by higher incentives).
  - Restructuring: Favorable adjustments from higher‑than‑expected retention on prior initiatives.
  - Operating income: Q2 rate up on higher gross margin and lower restructuring, partly offset by SG&A deleverage; 1H rate down on sales deleverage and incentives despite margin gains.
  - Store fleet and plans: Slight net decrease in Best Buy stores; growth in Yardbird; plan to close 20–30 Best Buy stores and open ~5 Outlets in FY24.

- International (Canada):
  - Revenue/Comps: Q2 $693M (-8.8%), comps -5.4%; 1H $1.36B (-10.2%), comps -5.5%; FX headwinds.
  - Category performance: Declines in home theater, large appliances, computing/tablets; growth in mobile phones, gaming, drones; services up on memberships/warranties.
  - Profitability: Gross margin rate up (mix and product margins); SG&A down (FX and lower store payroll) but operating margin down due to sales deleverage.
  - Stores: 160 total; modest net increase.

- Non‑GAAP results:
  - Q2 non‑GAAP operating income $362M (3.8% margin) vs $427M (4.1%); 1H $684M (3.6%) vs $912M (4.3%).
  - Non‑GAAP ETR increased (Q2 26.6% vs 16.7%; 1H 25.1% vs 20.8%).
  - Non‑GAAP diluted EPS decreased (Q2 $1.22 vs $1.54; 1H $2.37 vs $3.11).
  - Adjustments include intangible amortization, restructuring, investment loss, and gain on sale of a Mexico subsidiary; related tax effects detailed.

- Liquidity and capital resources:
  - Cash: $1.09B (down vs Jan 28, 2023; up vs prior year), with drivers including inventory timing, dividends, capex, and earnings.
  - Cash flows (1H): Operating $181M (improved vs prior‑year use), Investing $(381)M (lower capex, fewer investment purchases), Financing $(560)M (lower repurchases).
  - Capex outlook: ~ $850M for FY24.
  - Credit facility: New $1.25B unsecured revolver (undrawn) entered April 12, 2023; matures April 2028.
  - Credit ratings: S&P BBB+ Stable; Moody’s A3 Stable.

- Restricted cash: $398M (up YoY) primarily for product protection plans and self‑insurance; growth tied to paid memberships.

- Debt and capital: $1.15B notes outstanding (2028 and 2030 maturities).

- Capital returns:
  - Share repurchases: Q2 $69M; 1H $150M; authorization remaining under $5B program (no expiry). Expect higher repurchases in 2H FY24.
  - Dividends: Quarterly $0.92/share; cash dividends paid increased on higher rate, partly offset by fewer shares.

- Other financial measures: Current ratio 1.0; debt-to-earnings (TTM) 0.9 (up due to lower earnings).

- Off‑balance sheet and obligations: No material changes; undrawn revolver capacity noted.

- Accounting policies/estimates and new standards: No significant changes; no material impact expected from recent pronouncements.

- Safe harbor and risk factors: Forward‑looking statements subject to macro, competitive, operational, regulatory, and financial risks; references to Risk Factors in the 10‑K.

- Market risk:
  - Interest rates: Net asset exposure ~$1.0B (cash/restricted cash minus floating‑rate swapped debt); 50 bp change ~±$5M interest income.
  - FX: CAD weakness vs USD reduced reported revenue by ~$26M in Q2 and ~$72M in 1H; minimal earnings impact; limited use of FX forwards.

- Controls and procedures: Disclosure controls deemed effective; no material changes in internal control over financial reporting.

- Legal proceedings: Referenced to condensed consolidated financial statement notes.

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.heading: Item 3. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.start_phrase:
As disclosed in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 28, 2023, in addition to the risks inherent in our operations, we are exposed to 
certain market risks.
structure.summary:
- Market risk overview: Company faces interest rate and foreign currency risks.
- Interest rate risk:
  - Exposure through cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and debt partially swapped from fixed to floating.
  - As of July 29, 2023: $1.5 billion in cash/cash equivalents/restricted cash; $0.5 billion of debt swapped to floating; net asset position exposed to rates of $1.0 billion.
  - A 50-basis point change in short-term rates implies ±$5 million change in interest income.
- Foreign currency exchange rate risk:
  - Exposure primarily from International segment; limited use of foreign exchange forward contracts to hedge forecasted inventory purchases, recognized receivables/payables, and the investment in Canadian operations.
  - USD strength vs. CAD negatively impacted revenue: approximately $26 million unfavorable impact in Q2 FY2024 and $72 million for the first six months; impact on net earnings not significant.
- Controls and procedures:
  - Disclosure controls and procedures evaluated as effective as of July 29, 2023; overseen by a Disclosure Committee.
  - No changes in internal control over financial reporting during the fiscal quarter that materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, ICFR.
- Legal proceedings: Referenced to Note 10, Contingencies, in the 10-Q.

structure.title: Controls and Procedures
structure.heading: Item 4. Controls and Procedures
structure.start_phrase: We maintain disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in the reports we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’ s (“SEC”) rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Of ficer (principal executive officer) and Chief Financial Of ficer (principal financial of ficer), to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.
structure.summary:
- Market risk disclosures:
  - Interest rate risk: Exposure from cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and debt partially swapped to floating. As of July 29, 2023, $1.5 billion in cash and equivalents and $0.5 billion of debt swapped to floating, yielding a net $1.0 billion asset position sensitive to short-term rates. A 50-basis point move in short-term rates would change annualized interest income by approximately $5 million (increase if rates rise, decrease if rates fall). References prior 10-K Note 1 for swap details.
  - Foreign currency exchange rate risk: Exposure from International segment, primarily Canada; limited use of FX forwards for forecasted inventory purchases, recognized receivables/payables, and the Canadian investment. In Q2 and first six months of fiscal 2024, a stronger U.S. dollar versus the Canadian dollar reduced reported revenue by about $26 million (Q2) and $72 million (six months); impact on net earnings was not significant. References prior 10-K Note 1 for instruments.

- Controls and procedures:
  - Disclosure controls and procedures in place; a management Disclosure Committee meets regularly. Management (CEO and CFO) evaluated effectiveness as of July 29, 2023, and concluded controls were effective. No changes in internal control over financial reporting during the quarter that materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect ICFR.

- Other information:
  - Legal proceedings: See Note 10, Contingencies, in the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements.
  - Stock repurchases: Ongoing $5.0 billion authorization approved February 28, 2022, with no expiration. In Q2 fiscal 2024, repurchased 896,277 shares at an average price of $76.88. Period-end remaining authorization approximately $3.975 billion.
  - Rule 10b5-1 plans: No adoptions, terminations, or modifications by directors or officers during the quarter.

- Exhibits:
  - Corporate charter and by-laws (incorporated by reference).
  - CEO/CFO certifications under Sarbanes-Oxley Sections 302 and 906 (the latter not deemed “filed”).
  - iXBRL-formatted financial statements and cover page for the Q2 fiscal 2024 Form 10-Q.
  - Statement that certain immaterial long-term debt instruments are omitted under Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(4)(iii) and will be furnished to the SEC upon request.

structure.title: Other Information
structure.heading: Part II — Other Information
structure.summary:
- Stock repurchases: The board authorized a $5.0 billion share repurchase program on February 28, 2022, with no expiration. In the fiscal 2024 second quarter (Apr 30–Jul 29, 2023), the company repurchased 896,277 shares at an average price of $76.88, across three periods: 306,921 shares at $72.00; 334,957 shares at $77.22; and 254,399 shares at $82.30. All repurchases were under the publicly announced program. Approximately $3.975 billion remained available under the authorization at quarter-end. Additional details are referenced in Note 9 to the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements.
- Rule 10b5-1 plans: During the quarter ended July 29, 2023, no directors or officers adopted, terminated, or modified any Rule 10b5-1 or non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangements.
- Exhibits: The filing lists the Amended and Restated Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws (incorporated by reference), CEO and CFO certifications under Exchange Act Rules 13a-14(a)/15d-14(a) (SOX 302), and CEO/CFO certifications under 18 U.S.C. §1350 (SOX 906), with the 906 certifications furnished, not filed. It also includes iXBRL-formatted financial statements and the iXBRL cover page.
- Additional disclosure: Certain long-term debt instruments not exceeding 10% of total assets are omitted as exhibits pursuant to Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(4)(iii), with a commitment to furnish them to the SEC upon request.
